entry.title: Figma Plugin: Nearest Aspect Ratio Viewer
entry.summary:
Ever inspect a Figma frame and think… “what even is this ratio?” You’re not alone. Designers frequently run into frames with weird aspect ratios—things like 4:19 or 167:1000. And while that level of precision might be technically accurate, it's not exactly helpful if you’re trying to design consistently or prep assets for export. I built a tiny plugin to help. 👉 View it on Figma Community The Nearest Aspect Ratio plugin will: Analyze the selected frame or component Identify its actual aspect ratio Suggest the closest simple ratio (like 1:1, 4:3, 16:9, etc.) Recommend a simplified version (e.g. 4:19 becomes 1:5) Provide biased width/height conversions rounded to the nearest 25px for easier scaling If you’re designing a responsive layout, exporting assets, or prepping content for social media, having sensible ratios is helpful. Let’s say you want a layout to look “vertical.” A 3:4 or 9:16 frame is what you’re probably going for—but you end up with something like 347:982 and now you’re stuck trying to do math. This plugin does the math for you—and then politely rounds it to something a human can use. Here’s what the plugin gives back: Actual Ratio: 120:571 Nearest Clean Ratio: 1:5 Suggested Width: 200 (at height 1000) Suggested Height: 1125 (at width 225)
Now you can make fast decisions. Do you scale the frame down to 1:5? Or just rework the layout entirely? It’s the kind of plugin that helps remove a tiny mental load during the day. Select a frame in Figma. Run the plugin. Look at the left panel. Done. (Yes, really.) This was built mostly for myself, but maybe it helps you too. Let me know what would make it better. Should it let you adjust the size of the frame to match the new ratio? Should it include more “media” presets like A4 or Instagram story dimensions? Leave a comment or shoot a message. ✌️
Matt

entry.title: 👋 Hello Dev Community!
entry.summary:
We’re a group of high school students from Bhopal who created Cybersecurity Hub — a full-fledged website built for InfoSpark 2025, a national-level tech event. This wasn’t just about web development — it was about educating people, creating impact, and using code with a purpose. “In 2025, your biggest threat isn’t a virus — it’s a weak password, a careless click, or a phishing email disguised as homework.”
We saw our friends, classmates, even adults take online security lightly. So we set out to create something educational but engaging, interactive, and student-friendly — built by Gen Z, for Gen Z. 🧠 Myth-Breaking Login Page 🌐 Animated Home Page 📋 Security Tips Section 🧪 Password Strength Checker 📊 Charts Page 📈 Global cybercrime peaked at 160k+ reports
🇮🇳 India reported 80k+ incidents — and climbing fast
🎯 All built using: HTML, CSS, JavaScript
Chart.js
Pure DOM manipulation (no frameworks)
🔍 Challenges We Faced Designing the UI without any drag-and-drop tools — everything coded from scratch
Animating elements without slowing page load
Syncing register/login transitions smoothly
Making it run well on both mobile and PC
🧠 What We Learned (and You Can Too) CSS animations and transitions aren’t just cool — they engage users.
Entropy-based password scoring is more accurate than basic checks.
Good UI/UX can make even security education fun.
View it Yourself, https://github.com/Leonardoduty/CyberSecurity-Hub
